A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SIGS and contain readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices. Content can be matched across the substantial reformatting and experimental expansion.

before.justification: v2 reports original SIGS solution-discovery experiments, benchmark errors and runtimes, numerical convergence checks, and ablations in Section 3 and the appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical results and adds KdV, coupled-system, classical-solver, ChatGPT, and residual-comparison results in Section 3 and Appendices C.8–C.9.

M1.justification: v3 introduces a targeted SWE adaptation: aligning atom centers to the traveling-wave center before local coefficient refinement (C.8.2, Table 22). The grammar, TGVAE architecture and objectives, and core search Algorithms 1–4 remain unchanged.

E1.justification: v3 adds KdV soliton discovery without cosh/sech primitives, manufactured shallow-water systems, and steady compressible Euler systems. These introduce a missing-primitive scenario and coupled-field tasks beyond v2's retained scalar PDE coverage.

E2.justification: Tables 24–25 add Mathematica DSolveValue comparisons on five problems and ChatGPT with Extended Thinking on Burgers and PG-2. The original symbolic, neural, and FEniCS comparators remain. Coupled-system Table 28 reports SIGS results only.

E3.justification: The reported PG-2 convergence study changes from P4 elements on 16–128 meshes to P2 elements on 32–1024 meshes, with revised evaluation outputs. New experiments introduce coupled-system and CAS/LLM procedures. C.9 also introduces matched-accuracy timing, although its description conflicts with Table 27; retained P4 passages likewise leave some settings unresolved.

E4.justification: v3 adds the KdV missing-primitive robustness test, cross-mesh SIGS/FEniCS residual comparisons, and analysis of ChatGPT's boundary-condition failure, while replacing the FEniCS convergence analysis. Both original ablations remain; the TGVAE-versus-GVAE analysis moves to Appendix A.3.

E5.justification: The regularization ablation retains the same ten disjoint sample sets and uncertainty summaries, including 1486.2±19.5 versus 1433.2±27.3 decoding attempts. Training split seed 42 is unchanged. No new repeated-run or uncertainty-reporting practice is introduced.

E6.justification: New results include KdV error approximately 6.6e-6, SWE errors 0.0187–0.0418%, Euler errors 9.84–12.1%, and ChatGPT PG-2 error 157.6%, plus new convergence and residual measurements. Existing main accuracy tables are unchanged. Main timing entries change, such as diffusion from 39.2 to 14.67 seconds, but inconsistent accuracy alignment prevents interpreting these as same-setting speedups.

T1.justification: Appendix C.8 adds analytical verification of the recovered KdV expression through the sech/tanh identity, formal coupled-system definitions including the Euler equation of state, and Fourier/Green-function representations. The central grammar, regularization, and search mathematics remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction add explicit priority claims for solving coupled nonlinear systems and handling grammar misspecification, plus superiority to a CAS and reasoning LLM for unknown-solution problems. v2 emphasized general benchmark accuracy and efficiency without these expanded capability and priority claims.

C2.justification: v3 adds interpretations of alternative-expression synthesis, coupled-field recovery, and CAS/LLM failures, while qualifying grammar robustness as moderate misspecification. It softens the SSDE failure explanation to a hypothesis and changes the FEniCS convergence interpretation from O(h^5) to O(h).

D1.justification: v3 adds substantial problem-specific reproducibility information: coupled-field Ansätze, manufactured formulas and coefficients, parameter ranges, center adjustment, and comparator software/mode descriptions. Core training and hardware details remain. Conversely, v2's paragraph documenting the roughly 3-to-262-second epoch-time increase under topological regularization is removed.

R1.justification: The introduction replaces the inverse-problem symbolic-regression discussion and associated citations with classical analytical applications and references such as Ames, Debnath, and Natterer. CAS/LLM positioning is added, while the central relationship to HD-TLGP, SSDE, GVAEs, and PDE foundation models remains.

P1.justification: The abstract and introduction are substantially rewritten, the Ansatz explanation expands to contrast several solver families, and the experimental narrative is reorganized into numbered topics. The regularization ablation moves to Appendix A.3, and new appendix sections, acknowledgements, and an impact statement alter the document structure.

P2.justification: v3 adopts a two-column main layout, restacks Figure 1, redraws and reorders the main comparison plots, and changes color scales and legends. It adds an Ansatz table, coupled-field and ChatGPT figures, and several results tables, while restructuring the convergence and timing displays.

improvement.justification: The KdV, coupled-system, and residual studies substantially broaden v2's evidence. However, v3's SWE boundary/domain specifications disagree across Section 3, C.8.2, and Figure 11; C.4 mixes P2 and P4 descriptions; and C.9's matched-accuracy discussion contradicts Table 27. These inconsistencies affect the expanded generality and efficiency claims, preventing a reliable judgment of net overall improvement.
